analyst.summary: Cipla's FY26 record revenue (Rs 28,163cr) hides a real structural reset: EBITDA margin fell 25.9%->21.0% and PAT margin 19.1%->13.8% as North America revenue dropped 16.4% YoY to ~$780mn on the Revlimid patent cliff completing plus an unrelated OAI-driven production halt at its Lanreotide toll manufacturer in Greece -- two back-to-back quarters of 55-57% YoY PAT declines, confirmed independently in our own PIT data. Management's bridge (gAdvair/Symbicort respiratory launches, peptides, a $1bn US exit-run-rate target by FY27-end) is real but execution-dependent on FDA timelines that have already slipped once (Indore OAI since Nov-2023, still unresolved). What anchors the Hold call is India: a Rs 12,680cr, +9% YoY, chronic-led franchise carrying no US regulatory tail risk, sitting on a debt-free-grade balance sheet, with an orderly internal CEO succession (Achin Gupta, effective Apr-2026) and no fresh FDA escalation beyond two mild Form-483s at Goa in April 2026. At ~29.8x trailing PE the stock is not cheap, but the US reset is already known and largely priced, and the India-anchored quality base argues against selling into it.
